title: Which of the favors?
hookLine: the refrain of Surah ar-Rahman: which of your Lord's favors will you deny? (Quran 55)
tomorrow: a surah named for a borrowed cooking pot? why a pot?
last: MY OWN FRIEND · MODERATE · PRACTICE AND LETTING GO.

cards: A chorus is the part everyone knows by the second time through. The Quran has a surah built around one. It opens with a single name of God, ar-Rahman, the Beneficent.
Then come pictures of creation: the sun and the moon on their course, two seas that meet but don't mix, pearl and coral drawn out of them.
And between the pictures, the same line keeps coming back, in Pickthall's words: "Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny?"

teach.b: There's a story about how to answer it. A hadith in Tirmidhi's collection says the Prophet recited this surah to his companions, start to finish, and they stayed silent.
Then he told them the jinn had answered better. Each time he reached that line, they said: none of Your favors, our Lord, do we deny, and to You be praise. So the teaching is a habit of response.
The refrain isn't a scolding to sit under.

teach.h: A QUESTION THAT WANTS AN ANSWER.
teach.b: It's a question that wants an answer, out loud, every time it comes. Some Muslims still answer it that way when they hear the surah recited.
And the twist in this story: the ones who answered well weren't the people in the room. Ar-Rahman names its favors one picture at a time, sun, sea, pearl, and after each one it stops and asks.
In the hadith, the jinn answered every single one.

how: Surah ar-Rahman is often recited aloud for its rhythm and its refrain; some Muslims respond to the refrain with words of praise, following the hadith in Tirmidhi.

games.q: what does “which of the favors?” mean?
o: the refrain asking which of God's gifts you'd deny
a warning list of punishments for the ungrateful
a prayer said before eating to bless the food

s: the refrain of ar-Rahman is meant to make you feel guilty
in the hadith, the good response is praise: none of Your favors do we deny.
in a hadith, the jinn answered the refrain better than the companions
the companions stayed silent; the jinn answered every time the line came.
in the Gita, the self is a friend no matter what
this week's first line: the self is a friend to the one who has trained it.

games.q: your study group hears ar-Rahman recited in a video, and nobody says a word at the refrain. what does the hadith in Tirmidhi suggest?
o: answer it: none of Your favors do we deny, and to You be praise.
stay silent; the companions' silence was the respectful response.
skip ahead; the refrain repeats, so hearing it once is enough.
games.why: the companions were silent, and the Prophet said the jinn answered better, every time the line came.

practice: Count favors on your fingers, one per finger, small and plain: a bed, a meal, a voice that called. After each one, let a short pause be your answer. When you reach ten, start over if there's time.

wordCard.voice: Which of the favors? The refrain of Surah ar-Rahman, a question that asks to be answered.

orig.note: Arabic: the Beneficent, a name of God; the surah's first word and its name.

carryVoice: Carry this: which favor, counted out loud, one at a time. A full week: two books, seven lines.
